newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks close firm, tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks close firm, tracking Wall Street.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed broadly higher in erratic trade with the bolsa taking its cue from Wall Street's positive tilt, said dealers.
Foreign demand seen continuing Wednesday, although stocks prices could stumble if investors decide to cash in gains from the current rally, they said.
"Tomorrow there might be some profit-taking, but the bolsa will be very pegged to the U.S. market," said Nicolas Allende, a trader at ING Barings.
The 40-share ended up 0.3 percent at 117.46 points.
The general index gained 0.19 percent to 5,403.36 points on volume of 13.5 billion pesos.
The healthy turnover reflected a rise in buy orders from mutual funds and pension funds, which have been staying on the sidelines in recent sessions.
Gains included telecom stocks, which rose on an improvement in earnings in the highly competitive long- distance market, said Allende.
Entel, Chile's largest long-distance carrier, gained 2.11 percent to 2,900 pesos. Telex rose 1.29 percent to 1,180 pesos.
Losers included steel-maker Cap, down 0.88 percent at 1,130 pesos, power utility Enersis, down 0.55 percent at 269-1/2 pesos and pulp producer Copec, which rose 0.31 percent to 1,615 pesos.
